source.title: Bridging Functional and Representational Similarity via Usable Information

record.tranche_reason: The study empirically compares representational similarity measures and stitching outcomes, but does not test whether alignment rises with model scale or capability.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on stitching asymmetry, similarity under different transformation families, correlations between standard metrics and reconstruction-based similarity, task-granularity comparisons, and the relation between representational and functional similarity. The 58-model and 12,459-comparison totals describe experimental scope, not outcomes. Architecture and dataset details are in the appendices; the text gives conflicting descriptions of whether cross-architecture pairs were included in the experiments.
record.test_reason: This is a framework and validation paper, not a convergence study. Its results still bear on V6: the same vision-model representation pairs look more or less similar depending on the transformation family used to compare them, with a strict ordering for every pair. Its stitching-asymmetry result bears weakly on V4. It does not test scale, cross-modal, seed, universal-feature or cause-of-convergence questions.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that stitching loss estimates usable conditional information, so functional similarity needs bidirectional stitching. They further conclude that CKA, RSA and SVCCA act as empirical proxies for usable information under specific predictive families. They make no claim about whether models converge.
record.recipe_differences: Uses stitching accuracy ratios, reconstruction-based normalized MSE, and comparisons with CKA, RSA, and SVCCA; it does not reproduce a scale-alignment experiment from the cited original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Representational similarity increases with the expressiveness of the transformation family. Correlation with the reconstruction-based reference differs by metric: RSA and CKA are stronger than SVCCA.

fits_no_version.finding: High functional (stitching) similarity frequently occurs even when reconstruction-based representational similarity is low; high representational similarity implies high functional similarity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-level interchangeability between models can hold without global representational alignment, so stitching success overstates representational convergence.

fits_no_version.finding: Stitching similarity on coarse CIFAR-100 superclasses upper-bounds similarity on fine classes for the same representation pairs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Measured functional convergence depends on task granularity: coarser tasks make models look more alike.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 43rd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 306, 2026
record.problems: Empirical validation is restricted to supervised vision models; the standard-metric comparison is restricted to MLPs. Many plotted outcomes have no numeric values in the text. The paper describes the pairwise analysis inconsistently: Section 5 says cross-architecture stitching was filtered out, while Appendix C describes a cross-architecture grid. The authors also note sensitivity to optimization noise and threshold choices.

untested.parts: All: no scale or capability trend, and no cross-objective or cross-data comparison.
All: vision models only, no image-caption pairs.
Overall stitching success levels, cross-architecture stitching (excluded per Sec 5), relative representations, and mappings without paired data.
All: no neurons, SAE features or circuits.
Neighbour-count settings (no mutual-kNN), out-of-distribution inputs, and how dataset choice changes convergence conclusions.
All: no absolute alignment levels, plateau, or shared-data or objective explanations.

missing.what: Absolute representational-similarity levels per family, or a split by dataset or architecture group, needed to judge how complete alignment is.
A breakdown of stitching asymmetry by same-model versus different-model pairs, or by layer-depth gap.

record.verdict_notes: Section 5 and the Limitations say all comparisons were strictly intra-architecture (MLP-MLP, CNN-CNN). Appendix C instead describes cross-architecture stitching over a full N×M grid, e.g. ResNet-20 to MobileNetV3; the two accounts conflict. Layer pairs appear to include layers at different depths, and possibly layers within the same model, so the results are not clean between-model convergence measures. All key outcomes except the R² values are figure-only. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: Whether alignment rises with model size or capability, across different objectives or data, and across independently trained models.
Vision-language alignment on paired images and captions, and whether it rises with both models' performance.
Convergence across random initializations, shared features, or subspaces.

The study tests stitching and reconstruction-based mappings, but not relative representations, stitching of layers between different architectures as a consistent setting, or mappings without paired data.
Recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits.

It varies transformation-family capacity and compares metrics, but does not systematically vary neighbour count, test out-of-distribution inputs, or isolate the effect of changing datasets on the convergence result.
The experiments bear on incomplete alignment, but do not test whether alignment plateaus with scale or whether shared data or objectives cause it.

rows.measure: Distribution of directional stitching accuracy-ratio differences
rows.note: The text describes a peak at zero and heavy tails with significant variance, and says stitching is frequently asymmetric. The figure provides no extractable numeric values.
rows.check: The figure gives no numbers. The distribution peaks at zero but has heavy tails, and the pairs mix layers of different depths. The authors link the zero peak to adjacent layers, so the asymmetry partly reflects depth and information loss, not only cross-model mappability.

relationships.condition: Reconstruction-based similarity under orthogonal, orthogonal+scaling and affine families, all evaluated vision layer pairs
relationships.reason: Measured similarity rises strictly with family capacity for every pair; pairs distinct under Procrustes look near-identical under affine (R2–R4).
relationships.display_finding: Similarity increased strictly with mapping capacity for every evaluated layer pair, with pairs distinct under Procrustes appearing nearly identical under affine maps.

source_check.reason: R2–R4 and Section 5.2 establish strictly increasing similarity with family capacity for every individual pair. This supports the comparison-family component of V6.

relationships.condition: Standard metrics versus orthogonal+scaling reconstruction similarity, MLP pairs only
relationships.reason: CKA and RSA agree closely with the reference (R2 0.937, 0.912), so metric choice matters little there; only SVCCA diverges (R2 0.650) (R5–R7).
relationships.display_finding: Agreement with the reconstruction reference reached R²=0.937 for CKA and 0.912 for RSA, compared with 0.650 for SVCCA.

source_check.condition: Standard metrics versus orthogonal+scaling reconstruction similarity, MLP pairs only
source_check.reason: R5–R6 establish strong correlation, not negligible changes in similarity or absence of metric dependence. R7 reports moderate agreement and divergence, consistent with dependence. These results do not establish the claimed limiting condition.

The authors-conclusion paraphrase is supported; scale trends, input-distribution dependence, and convergence across training are untested.

statements.correction: MLP pairs only; reference=orthogonal-plus-isotropic-scaling reconstruction similarity; CKA R²=0.937; RSA R²=0.912; both p<0.001. Strong correlation supports agreement as proxies, without establishing negligible metric dependence.
statements.problem: The MLP results and substantial agreement are correctly reported, but their framing as limits_scope overstates what correlation establishes about metric dependence.
